headline: Broad-based growth beats guidance, full-year outlook raised
summary_short: Howmet Aerospace's Q2 2026 revenue rose 24.1% y/y to $2,547M (21% organic), with Adjusted EBITDA margin up 340bp to 32.1% and Adjusted EPS up 46.2% to $1.33 — all above the high end of prior guidance. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised across revenue, EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow.
summary_long: Growth was broad-based: commercial aerospace +28%, defense aerospace +11%, gas turbines +38% y/y, lifting revenue 24% (21% organic, ex-CAM/Brunner/Savannah). Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 340bp to 32.1% despite absorbing the newly-closed CAM acquisition. GAAP operating income rose 36.5% y/y to $711M, but fell q/q from $753M since Q1 2026 included a one-time $93M restructuring credit (Savannah gain) absent in Q2. Cash fell to $563M from $2,435M q/q on the ~$1.8B CAM close, a $186M debt paydown, and $300M buybacks. Free cash flow was $479M (+39% y/y) after $104M capex. FY2026 guidance raised: revenue +$400M to $10,050M baseline, Adjusted EBITDA +$170M to $3,230M, Adjusted EPS +$0.33 to $5.27, FCF +$150M to $1,900M. Q3 dividend raised 17% to $0.14/share.

drivers.explanation: Revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA margin, and Adjusted EPS all exceeded the high end of guidance, per CEO John Plant, with all major end markets in growth mode.
Growth driven by 28% commercial aerospace, 11% defense aerospace, and 38% gas turbines market growth; organic growth was 21% excluding the CAM, Brunner, and Savannah transactions.
340bp y/y expansion to 32.1%, which the company says includes absorbing the CAM fastener acquisition closed in April.
Q2 2026's $711M is up 36.5% y/y, but the $753M-to-$711M q/q decline is mechanically explained by a $93M one-time restructuring credit (Savannah gain) booked in Q1 2026 that did not recur in Q2.
Cash fell q/q mainly from closing the ~$1.8B CAM acquisition in April, plus a $186M Japanese Yen term-loan repayment and $300M of common stock repurchases in the quarter.
Cash from operations of $583M against $104M capex; the release attributes the strength to overall cash generation without a specific line-item cause.
